pharm-msk:aa.q: Aspirin's antiplatelet effect comes from blocking:
pharm-msk:aa.e: Irreversible COX acetylation; platelets cannot make new enzyme.

pharm-msk:aa.q: A 42-year-old woman with asthma and nasal polyps develops wheezing, rhinorrhea and flushing within an hour of taking ibuprofen. Skin testing for drug allergy is negative. Mechanism of her reaction?
pharm-msk:aa.e: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease: COX blockade diverts arachidonic acid to the 5-lipoxygenase pathway (↑ cysteinyl leukotrienes). It is not IgE-mediated.

pharm-msk:apap.q: Acetaminophen differs from NSAIDs because it:
Why is acetaminophen preferred for fever in children with viral illness?
o: It carries no risk of Reye syndrome
It shortens the course of viral illness
pharm-msk:apap.e: Unlike aspirin, which is avoided in children with viral infections.

pharm-msk:apap.q: A 70-year-old woman with stage 3 chronic kidney disease and a past bleeding duodenal ulcer needs regular analgesia for hip osteoarthritis. The preferred first-line drug acts mainly by:
o: Central COX inhibition, weak peripheral effect
pharm-msk:apap.e: Acetaminophen inhibits COX centrally, so it lacks NSAID renal, GI and antiplatelet effects. Selective COX-2 inhibitors still impair renal prostaglandins.

pharm-msk:aspirin.q: Aspirin is avoided in children with viral illness because of:

o: Secondary prevention of MI and stroke

pharm-msk:aspirin.q: A 58-year-old man with acute chest pain and ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF is given 325 mg of chewable aspirin. How long does a single dose impair platelet function?
o: About 24 hours, until COX is resynthesized
About 6 hours, until the drug is cleared
pharm-msk:aspirin.e: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates COX-1, and anucleate platelets cannot make new enzyme, so the effect lasts for the platelet's lifespan.

o: Makes it safe in sulfa allergy
pharm-msk:coxib.e: But ↑ thrombotic risk; sulfa allergy cross-reaction.

pharm-msk:coxib.q: Why do COX-2 inhibitors raise CV risk?
A 64-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis and a prior upper GI bleed is switched from naproxen to celecoxib. Which adverse effect is increased by this drug's COX-2 selectivity?
pharm-msk:coxib.e: COX-2 inhibition lowers endothelial prostacyclin while platelet thromboxane A₂ is spared, favoring thrombosis. Sparing COX-1 reduces, not increases, GI bleeding.

pharm-msk:nsaids.e: Prostaglandins dilate the afferent arteriole; NSAIDs also cause interstitial nephritis.
PGE₁ (alprostadil) keeps it open; indomethacin is also a tocolytic.

pharm-msk:nsaids.q: A 62-year-old man takes low-dose aspirin after a myocardial infarction. For knee pain he begins ibuprofen, which he takes each morning about 30 minutes before his aspirin. Why may this reduce his cardioprotection?
o: Ibuprofen blocks aspirin's access to COX-1
pharm-msk:nsaids.e: Ibuprofen reversibly occupies the platelet COX-1 channel and prevents aspirin from irreversibly acetylating Ser529, so thromboxane A₂ synthesis recovers as ibuprofen dissociates. Aspirin should be taken ≥ 30 min before (or 8 h after) ibuprofen.

pharm-msk:dmards.q: Methotrexate in RA requires supplementation with:
A 40-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis takes a weekly oral DMARD but skipped her folic acid. She develops oral ulcers and pancytopenia with an MCV of 108 fL. The drug acts by inhibiting:
pharm-msk:dmards.e: Methotrexate inhibits DHFR, causing megaloblastic cytopenias and mucositis prevented by folate supplementation. Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase is inhibited by leflunomide.

pharm-msk:bisph.e: Pyrophosphate analogs bind hydroxyapatite and inhibit osteoclast-mediated resorption.

pharm-msk:bisph.q: Oral alendronate is taken upright with water to avoid:
pharm-msk:bisph.e: Also jaw osteonecrosis and atypical femur fractures.

pharm-msk:bisph.q: A 70-year-old woman takes a weekly oral tablet for osteoporosis, swallowed upright with a full glass of water. After a tooth extraction she has exposed, necrotic mandibular bone that will not heal. The drug acts by:
o: Selective estrogen receptor modulation in bone
Activation of calcitonin receptors on osteoclasts
Intermittent activation of the PTH receptor
pharm-msk:bisph.e: Alendronate (a bisphosphonate) binds bone mineral and inhibits osteoclast resorption; osteonecrosis of the jaw is a known adverse effect. Raloxifene is a SERM associated with VTE, not jaw osteonecrosis.

pharm-msk:anabolic.e: Given intermittently, which stimulates osteoblasts; risk of osteosarcoma in rodents.
Inhibits osteoclast formation; romosozumab targets sclerostin.

pharm-msk:anabolic.q: A 74-year-old woman with a T-score of −3.4 has new vertebral fractures despite alendronate. Her physician plans daily subcutaneous injections of a drug that stimulates osteoblasts. Which history would contraindicate this drug?
o: Myocardial infarction or stroke in the past year
Paget disease of bone or prior skeletal radiation
Prior deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism
pharm-msk:anabolic.e: Teriparatide (PTH analog) carries an osteosarcoma concern, so it is avoided in Paget disease or prior bone radiation. Recent MI/stroke is the caution for romosozumab.

pharm-msk:goutchronic.q: A 55-year-old kidney transplant recipient taking azathioprine has recurrent gout with tophi. Allopurinol is started. Unless the azathioprine dose is reduced, the combination risks:
pharm-msk:goutchronic.e: Xanthine oxidase inactivates 6-mercaptopurine (azathioprine's active metabolite); allopurinol blocks this, raising levels and causing myelosuppression.

pharm-msk:goutacute.q: Which drug should not be started during an acute flare?
pharm-msk:goutacute.e: Starting it can prolong the flare; continue it if the patient is already taking it.
Inhibits URAT1 urate reabsorption; risk of uric acid stones.

pharm-msk:goutacute.q: A 62-year-old man with an eGFR of 25 mL/min and a recent bleeding gastric ulcer has a hot, swollen knee; aspirate shows negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals and no organisms. Most appropriate treatment for this flare?
pharm-msk:goutacute.e: Acute gout with severe CKD and GI bleeding: glucocorticoids are preferred. NSAIDs are contraindicated here, and urate-lowering drugs do not treat a flare.

pharm-msk:tnf.q: Before starting a TNF-α inhibitor, screen for:
pharm-msk:tnf.e: Reactivation of TB is the classic risk.
Decoy receptor for TNF-α; infliximab, adalimumab, golimumab are anti-TNF antibodies.

pharm-msk:tnf.q: A 45-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis started infliximab 4 months ago. She now has fever, night sweats, weight loss and an apical cavitary lesion; sputum shows acid-fast bacilli. Why did this infection develop?
o: Loss of TNF-α needed to maintain granulomas
pharm-msk:tnf.e: TNF-α is essential for forming and maintaining granulomas that contain M. tuberculosis, so blockade reactivates latent TB. Complement C5 blockade predisposes to Neisseria infection.

pharm-msk:psobio.e: Used in psoriasis and Crohn disease; guselkumab targets IL-23 p19.

pharm-msk:psobio.q: A 34-year-old man has extensive plaque psoriasis not controlled by topical therapy. He also has Crohn disease. Which biologic should be avoided?
pharm-msk:psobio.e: IL-17A inhibitors such as secukinumab can trigger or worsen inflammatory bowel disease. Ustekinumab and anti-TNF agents treat both psoriasis and Crohn disease.

pharm-msk:imiq.e: Stimulates a local immune response; used for genital warts, actinic keratosis and superficial BCC.

pharm-msk:imiq.q: A 27-year-old woman has multiple soft, flesh-colored, cauliflower-like anogenital papules caused by HPV types 6 and 11. She is prescribed a topical immune response modifier that she applies herself. Its mechanism is:
pharm-msk:imiq.e: Imiquimod activates TLR7, inducing interferon-α and a local antiviral immune response against condylomata. Thymidylate synthase inhibition is 5-fluorouracil.

pharm-msk:ra-bio.e: Used in RA and giant cell arteritis.
CTLA-4–Ig binds B7, preventing CD28 engagement.

pharm-msk:ra-bio.q: A 74-year-old woman has new temporal headache, jaw claudication and ESR of 92 mm/h. Temporal artery biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells. A steroid-sparing biologic is added. Its target is:
pharm-msk:ra-bio.e: Giant cell arteritis: tocilizumab (anti-IL-6 receptor) reduces glucocorticoid exposure. Rituximab targets CD20 and is used in RA and ANCA vasculitis.

pharm-msk:skinmap.e: Oral retinoid for severe nodulocystic acne.

pharm-msk:skinmap.q: A 30-year-old man has well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale on his elbows and knees. He is prescribed topical calcipotriene. Excessive use over large areas can cause:
pharm-msk:skinmap.e: Calcipotriene is a vitamin D analog; extensive application can raise serum calcium. Skin atrophy is the classic effect of potent topical steroids.

pharm-msk:tcs.q: Adverse effect of long-term potent topical steroids:
pharm-msk:tcs.e: Avoid potent steroids on face and skin folds.

pharm-msk:tcs.q: Topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus) are useful on the face because:
o: They do not cause skin atrophy
They are cheaper than topical steroids
They also act as topical antibiotics

pharm-msk:tcs.q: A 6-year-old boy has recurrent itchy, lichenified eczema on his eyelids and face. His mother wants to avoid steroid-induced skin thinning. The preferred topical agent acts by:
pharm-msk:tcs.e: Topical tacrolimus/pimecrolimus inhibit calcineurin and do not cause atrophy, making them ideal for facial atopic dermatitis. Glucocorticoid receptor agonism is the steroid mechanism.

o: A single pregnancy test at baseline only
No testing if using oral contraceptives
pharm-msk:acne.e: iPLEDGE program; also monitor lipids and LFTs.

o: Blocking androgen receptors in the skin
Agonism at nuclear retinoic acid receptors
pharm-msk:acne.e: Reduces resistance when combined with topical antibiotics.

pharm-msk:acne.q: A 17-year-old girl has severe nodulocystic acne with scarring despite oral doxycycline and topical retinoids. She is started on oral isotretinoin with two forms of contraception and monthly pregnancy tests. Which other labs must be monitored?
pharm-msk:acne.e: Isotretinoin raises triglycerides and can elevate transaminases. TPMT is checked before azathioprine, not retinoids.

pharm-msk:psotop.q: Methotrexate in psoriasis requires monitoring for:

pharm-msk:psotop.e: Prolonged teratogenicity — pregnancy must be avoided for years after use.

pharm-msk:psotop.q: A 35-year-old woman has a few well-demarcated, silvery-scaled plaques on her elbows and knees covering about 2% of body surface area. No joint symptoms. Most appropriate initial therapy?
pharm-msk:psotop.e: Limited plaque psoriasis is treated first with topical corticosteroids (± a vitamin D analog). Systemic methotrexate is reserved for extensive disease or arthritis.

pharm-msk:ra.q: Anchor drug for most patients with early RA:
Low-dose glucocorticoids in RA are used as:
o: Bridging therapy until DMARDs take effect
A cure for established joint erosions

pharm-msk:ra.q: A 29-year-old woman with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis and active synovitis of the MCP joints plans to conceive within the next year. Which DMARD is most appropriate?
pharm-msk:ra.e: Hydroxychloroquine (and sulfasalazine) is compatible with pregnancy. Methotrexate and leflunomide are teratogenic and must be stopped well before conception.

pharm-msk:oa-op.q: First-line drug therapy for knee OA:

A 67-year-old woman has bilateral knee pain that worsens with activity, morning stiffness under 20 minutes and crepitus. X-rays show asymmetric joint space narrowing and osteophytes. Most appropriate initial drug?
pharm-msk:oa-op.e: Osteoarthritis: topical NSAIDs (with exercise and weight loss) are first line. Methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine treat inflammatory arthritis, not OA.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: นิ้วโป้งเท้าบวมแดง
title.en: Boss case: The red, swollen big toe

boss.case: A 50-year-old man wakes at 3 a.m. with an exquisitely painful, red, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint after a night of beer and seafood. He takes hydrochlorothiazide. Joint aspirate: needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals.

qs.q: First-line treatment of the acute flare:
qs.e: e.g., indomethacin. Urate-lowering drugs are not started to treat the flare.

o: Inhibiting URAT1 urate reabsorption in the proximal tubule
Inhibiting xanthine oxidase in urate production
qs.e: Binds tubulin. Diarrhea is the commonest side effect.

qs.q: Which medication contributes to his hyperuricemia?
qs.e: Thiazides and loop diuretics reduce urate excretion; losartan is uricosuric.
Xanthine oxidase inhibitor; titrate to urate < 6 mg/dL.

qs.q: Before starting allopurinol in patients of Han Chinese or Thai descent, test for:

title.th: ข้อมือข้อนิ้วฝืดตอนเช้า

stem.en: A 42-year-old woman has 3 months of symmetric swelling of the MCPs and wrists with > 1 hour of morning stiffness.

info.th: RF และ anti-CCP บวก

steps.e: Or another biologic or a JAK inhibitor.

steps.q: Before the biologic, she must be screened for:
